candidate.desc: You can turn pressure into a clear next step. When a plan falls apart, you can cut the problem down to the part that needs attention first.

original.desc: The day everything breaks is the day you are calmest. Others freeze. You are already cutting the problem into pieces that can be solved.

candidate.desc: You can keep shaping a project after the first excitement passes. Each careful cut leaves the useful work intact, so the next attempt can build on what is already there.

original.desc: You cut so the thing can grow. What you plant and keep cutting back, money, skill, trust, comes back with interest because you never let it sprawl.

candidate.desc: You can give an idea a clean edge without making the telling feel like work. A few plain words let someone else pick it up and use it.

original.desc: What is inside you moves outward without forcing. When you speak, you say the thing the table has been talking around, and the answer comes back plain.
